To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the lateral wave, the Norton wave, and the surface waves are the dominant features of the near-earth wave propagation for the two-layer medium.

(i) the lateral wave is the dominant propagation mechanism for the case of both transmitter and receiver located above the dielectrics layer, (ii) the Norton wave is significant for the case of either transmitter or receiver located above the layer, and (iii) the pole contribution is negligible for the case of transmitter and receiver both located above the layer. the lateral wave, though it may be highly localized near the interface, is an important propagation feature in the presence of the dielectric layer and that the Norton wave is a significant contribution when both the dipole and the observation point are above the dielectric medium or when one is within and the other is above the layer.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a study of the near-earth propagation characteristics of an electric dipole in a two-layer medium.
the development of a computational efficient solution to the problem of near-earth propagation in the presence a dielectric layer.
the development of a computationally efficient, analytical solution to the two-layer propagation model for near-earth propagation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the Norton wave is a significant contribution to the total field when the dipole is above the dielectric, the observation point is below the dielectric layer and when the dipole or observation point is above the dielectrics layer and the other is below it.
, for a given source and observation point location configuration, the lateral wave is the dominant contribution to the total field for the two-layer case.
the lateral wave is a significant propagation feature only when both source and observation points are below the dielectric layer.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, in general, for near-field propagation problems, the Norton wave must be included in the solution, and the lateral wave is significant when the dipole is above the dielectric interface.

the Norton and lateral waves are the two most important contributions to the near-earth wave propagation characteristics of an electric dipole, and the Norton wave, in particular, is a significant contributor to the field when the dipole is located above the layer.
the lateral wave is a significant propagation feature in the two-layer environment when the source and receiver are both located above or within the layer.
The main takeaway from our work is that
for a given source and observation point, there is a unique set of propagation features that are present in all of the electric field components.
the Norton wave can be used as a tool to identify a dielectric layer.
the Norton wave is an important feature for the two-layer problem, even for the cases where the dipole and/or observation point are located above the dielectrical layer.
